nodes.title: Pressing onward in spiritual maturity
nodes.summary: Uses Philippians 3:12-14 to show that Paul continues pursuing Christ and refuses to remain spiritually static.

nodes.title: Follow a pattern of continued maturity
nodes.summary: Uses Philippians 3:15-17 to urge humility about progress and practice the example of those faithfully following Christ.

nodes.summary: Applies Paul’s pursuit of Christ to Scripture study, removal of idols and rejection of excuses for stagnation. A personal gym learning illustration appears in spoken elaboration.

nodes.title: Iron sharpens iron
nodes.summary: Treats Proverbs 27:17 as an image for mutual discipleship, godly correction, and reciprocal spiritual growth.

nodes.title: Biblical examples of interpersonal correction
nodes.summary: Cites Nathan confronting David, Paul confronting Peter, disagreement between Barnabas and Paul, Euodia and Syntyche, and Timothy as examples; these are reported illustrations, not additional formal sermon RSS references.

nodes.title: Restore with gentleness and self-watchfulness
nodes.summary: Uses Galatians 6:1 to insist correction be offered with grace and gentleness while examining one’s own vulnerability to temptation.

nodes.title: Do not use keeping the peace to avoid needed correction
nodes.summary: Rebukes passivity that overlooks sin in fellow believers and urges compassionate, biblically grounded accountability; Pastor Jacob includes himself in the criticism.

nodes.title: Teach about sin for genuine church growth
nodes.summary: Argues that removing calls to repentance may draw attendance without producing discipleship; presents the contrary pastoral conviction that preaching on sin is necessary for healthy growth.

nodes.title: A sharp church does not depend only on the pulpit
nodes.summary: Concludes that accountability and Scripture-shaped discipleship belong among believers, not only in pastoral preaching; asks whether the congregation has grown dull.

nodes.title: A spiritually serious congregation can serve its city
nodes.summary: Calls the Cedar Grove congregation to active participation in the gospel witness of Lebanon and closes toward the Lord’s Supper.

discover.question: What does accountability mean in the Cedar Grove core values?
discover.answer: Taking responsibility before Christ and growing mutually with other believers. The sermon states both relationships as a single church-core-value commitment.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: What are the two dimensions of Christian accountability?
discover.answer: First, believers are accountable for their own walk with Christ; second, they are accountable to fellow believers in the church family.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: Why does gathering with the church matter in Hebrews 10?
discover.answer: Pastor Jacob uses Hebrews 10:23-25 to connect gathering with stirring one another to love and good works, not simply fulfilling an attendance obligation.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: How does Philippians 2:2 shape the response to friction in church?
discover.answer: The sermon urges believers to examine their own hearts, remembering that congregations consist of people growing at different rates.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: How does the sermon explain justification?
discover.answer: God declares a sinner righteous by grace through faith in Jesus Christ; Romans 3:10 and Romans 5:1 anchor the contrast between sinful condition and peace with God.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: How is sanctification different from justification?
discover.answer: Sanctification is the ongoing, holy transformation of a believer. Pastor Jacob uses 1 Thessalonians 4:3-7 and the Greek term hagiasmos.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: How does the sermon describe glorification?
discover.answer: It is the final removal of sin and complete conformity to Christ, not becoming a god; the sermon connects this hope to 2 Corinthians 4:17-18.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: Why does Paul press on in Philippians 3 even after years in ministry?
discover.answer: Pastor Jacob stresses continuing to know Christ rather than treating spiritual growth as finished, using Philippians 3:12-17.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: What practical habits hinder spiritual growth?
discover.answer: The sermon challenges excuses, lack of Bible study, and competing priorities that crowd out daily time knowing Jesus.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: What does it mean that Christ must have first place?
discover.answer: Colossians 1:18 is used to ask whether Jesus truly has priority and Lordship over a believer’s life.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: What is the meaning of iron sharpening iron?
discover.answer: Proverbs 27:17 illustrates believers helping and correcting one another toward spiritual maturity and accountability.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: How should correction be given according to Galatians 6:1?
discover.answer: With gentleness, grace and personal humility, seeking restoration rather than excusing sin or attacking the offender.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: Why can keeping the peace become an excuse?
discover.answer: Pastor Jacob warns that avoidance of necessary biblical correction can let harmful habits go unaddressed in the congregation.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

discover.question: What must accompany preaching to make a church spiritually healthy?
discover.answer: The sermon says mutual accountability and discipleship must happen across the body, not only from the pulpit.
discover.answerOrigin: ANALYSIS — SYNTHESIS from Pastor Jacob spoken and prepared teaching

authorCorpus.purpose: Private long-term Pastor Jacob Lannom teaching/research corpus; not a voice-cloning or invented-authoritative-text source.
recurringTheses: The church should feel like a family without denying the need for growth and correction.
Personal accountability requires continual spiritual growth under Christ’s Lordship.
Justification, sanctification, and glorification frame the work of salvation over time.
Scripture study and spiritual priorities matter to Christian maturity.
Mutual accountability must pursue restoration with gentleness rather than mere avoidance of conflict.
Proclaiming truth about sin and practicing discipleship are essential to a healthy congregation.
potentialLiteraryDestinations: local church covenant and core values
